children: Jaipur’s Grade A warehousing market records 22 per cent vacancy, with 2.4 million sq. ft of additional supply projected by 2028

Jaipur is emerging as one of India’s more active Tier 2 commercial real estate markets, with office, retail and warehousing segments recording steady expansion, according to JLL. The city’s growth reflects increasing business interest beyond traditional metropolitan markets.

The city’s proximity to Delhi-NCR, improving infrastructure and comparatively lower operating costs have supported its emergence as a commercial destination. These factors are attracting businesses looking to expand operations while accessing the region’s growing talent pool at competitive costs.

Jaipur’s office market currently has 9.70 million sq. ft of operational stock, catering to occupiers across IT/ITES, BFSI, consulting and other sectors. Office rents in the city range between Rs 45 and Rs 95 per sq. ft per month.

The flexible workspace segment has around 11,000 operational seats, while another 3,150 seats are expected to be added over the next few quarters. The city is also projected to receive 3.32 million sq. ft of additional office supply by 2028.

“Jaipur exemplifies the transformation underway across North India’s Tier 2 markets. We are witnessing occupier demand from technology firms, financial institutions, and logistics operators who recognise that Jaipur offers the infrastructure quality of metro markets with superior cost economics and access to North India’s expanding talent base,” said Manish Aggarwal, Senior Managing Director, North and East India, JLL.

According to Aggarwal, the flexible workspace segment is expanding, while planned supply additions indicate continued developer confidence in the market. The combination of occupier demand, infrastructure and cost economics is supporting Jaipur’s positioning among emerging commercial markets.

Jaipur’s office market is spread across three broad business districts, catering to different occupier requirements. The Central Business District includes MI Road and C Scheme, while the Secondary Business District covers Civil Lines, Ajmer Road, Vidyadhar Nagar, Malviya Nagar, Tonk Road and JLN Marg.

The Peripheral Business District includes Mahindra City, Jagatpura and Sitapura and has emerged as a major growth corridor for technology and IT-enabled services. Mahindra SEZ hosts anchor occupiers such as Wipro and Infosys, while Sitapura and Jagatpura have recorded leasing momentum.

The three-district structure allows Jaipur to accommodate different categories of commercial demand, ranging from premium corporate requirements in established locations to technology-led expansion in peripheral areas. Competitive rents and newer infrastructure are supporting activity across the emerging corridors.

Jaipur has around 4.9 million sq. ft of organised mall stock across approximately 12 operational projects, with vacancy at about 16 per cent. Premium retail space commands rents ranging between Rs 100 and Rs 280 per sq. ft per month.

The city is expected to add another 0.9 million sq. ft of mall space by 2028. The planned supply, alongside the existing organised retail base, indicates continued development of the city’s retail market and its ability to accommodate national and global brands.

Jaipur’s Grade A warehousing stock stands at 3.5 million sq. ft, with rents ranging between Rs 18 and Rs 24 per sq. ft per month. Vacancy in the segment is around 22 per cent, while another 2.4 million sq. ft of supply is expected to enter the market by 2028.

Industrial and warehousing activity is concentrated across three primary zones. Sikar Road-NH 11 and the VKI Area command rents of Rs 19-24 per sq. ft per month, while Ajmer Road-NH 48 records rents of Rs 20-25.

The Malviya Nagar-Sitapura Industrial Area has rents ranging between Rs 22 and Rs 25 per sq. ft per month. Together, these corridors form the city’s key industrial and logistics network and provide locations for businesses seeking relatively competitive commercial and operational costs.
